name: theme-studio-edit-reaches-the-window
description: A live edit made in the Settings > Spaces studio has to reach the browser window behind it, and Save has to persist it. The fixture's one space starts with a low-opacity gradient (0.3) already in themes.json, so the studio opens on a real theme rather than the absent-theme case. The scenario opens Settings, selects the Spaces pane and the space, drags the opacity slider to 1.0 (an eval that sets the range input's value and dispatches `input`, the same mechanism a real drag produces), and reads back BrowserController::PreviewSpaceTheme's own log line. Before Save it also captures the settings window itself with the Theme section open, and reads the section's own control count (theme-studio.js's SLIDERS list draws 6 range inputs - opacity, grain, vignette, frost, warmth, darkAdaptation - plus one gradient canvas) - nobody had seen the studio rendered until this. It then clicks Save and reads AtriumSettingsWindow::OnThemeSaved's line, closes the settings window with Cmd+W (routing-pane-adds-a-rule.json's route back to the key browser window), and pixel-compares the window's own backdrop from before the edit to after it - both captures taken with the settings window closed, so neither frame is occluded by it.

actions.note: gate: the startup tab committed, so the app and the fixture are live
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
the window's own backdrop, the fixture's opacity-0.3 gradient, before any studio edit

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="spaces"]'); if (!b) return 'no-pane'; b.click(); return document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="spaces"].selected') ? 'selected' : 'not-selected'; })()
actions.note: the Spaces pane in the rail, selected by data-pane rather than a coordinate

actions.expression: (() => { const item = document.querySelector('.settings-space-item[data-space="0"]'); if (!item) return 'no-item'; item.click(); const after = document.querySelector('.settings-space-item[data-space="0"]'); return after && after.classList.contains('selected') ? 'selected' : 'not-selected'; })()
actions.note: the fixture's one space, in the master-detail list

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector('.theme-studio-slider[data-key="opacity"]'); if (!el) return 'no-slider'; el.value = '1'; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); return 'set:' + el.value; })()
actions.note: THE EDIT: the opacity slider, set the way a real drag ends - a new value on the input, then the same `input` event theme-studio.js listens for
BrowserController::PreviewSpaceTheme's own line - the edit reached a realised Atrium window
let the repaint settle before the next capture
the settings window is the last one this scenario touched, but CDP evals never move macOS window ordering - reassert Atrium frontmost so the studio capture below actually shows the settings window

actions.expression: (() => { const section = document.querySelector('.settings-theme-section'); if (!section) return 'no-section'; const sliders = section.querySelectorAll('input[type="range"]').length; const canvas = !!section.querySelector('canvas'); return 'sliders=' + sliders + ' canvas=' + canvas; })()
actions.note: records the studio's own presence before Save: how many range sliders theme-studio.js drew inside the Theme section, and whether its gradient canvas exists
the settings window with the Theme section open and the opacity slider already bumped, taken before Save - nobody had seen the studio itself rendered until this

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.theme-studio-save'); if (!b) return 'no-save'; b.click(); return 'clicked'; })()

actions.note: AtriumSettingsWindow::OnThemeSaved's line - the edit reached themes.json, not just the live preview
closes the key Settings window and hands key back to the browser window - routing-pane-adds-a-rule.json's own route, since cmd+t would open a tab in whichever window is key
re-assert the browser window frontmost now that Settings is closed
the window's own backdrop after the saved edit, with Settings closed so nothing occludes it

assertions.desc: the Spaces pane was reachable from the rail
the fixture's space was there to select
the opacity slider took the new value
the studio drew all 6 sliders (opacity, grain, vignette, frost, warmth, darkAdaptation - theme-studio.js's own SLIDERS list) and its gradient canvas, visible in the frame captured this same moment
the Save button was there to click
Settings closed with Cmd+W, so only the browser window is left before the quit
the opacity edit reached the window's own backdrop (raw-pixel region compare over the sidebar margin, same region presenter-startup.json uses)
Cmd+Q still quits cleanly after a settings edit and a save
